questions.question: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents this; a new holder receives it Oathkeeper-side. At end of round eight an existing Usurper can win under the ordered endgame rules.

required_facts.expected_fact: Victory is checked before the next-Wake Oathkeeper-to-Usurper flip; ordinary Usurper victory is at the following Wake if retained.
An existing Usurper can instead win at the end-of-round-eight priority check, potentially before the following Wake.
Losing the title prevents that win; transfer/retaking uses the Oathkeeper side and restarts the sequence.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: Taking the title during Act does not permit an immediate Usurper win: at the next Wake the title is still Oathkeeper-side and is checked before it flips; after it flips, the first Usurper check is the following Wake, or round-eight end if that comes first. Losing the title prevents the win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

reader-b.answer: After taking Oathkeeper during Act, at next Wake the Exile is checked before the title flips, so cannot yet win as Usurper; title then flips to Usurper. They can first win at the following Wake, or at round 8 end if still Usurper and that arrives first. Losing title prevents it; regaining resets the sequence.
evidence: Citizen succession is a separate test

questions.fixed_expected_answer: Supremacy/Conquest: most sites; People/Rebellion: People’s Favor; Protection/Sanctuary: most relics and banners combined; Devotion/Faith: Darkest Secret. Exile must have the Vision revealed, fulfill it at Wake (or the round-eight check), and at least three Visions must have been drawn from the world deck. Most means strictly more than every other player, not a tie.

questions.question: At round eight, what is the complete victory priority including simultaneous Visions and Citizens?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Empire if Chancellor/Citizen Oathkeeper, then Exile Usurper, then qualifying Exile Visionary (Conquest > Rebellion > Sanctuary > Faith), then Empire fallback. Each Empire win is Chancellor unless a Citizen fulfills the Successor goal, who wins alone instead.

required_facts.expected_fact: At automatic round-eight ending: Imperial Oathkeeper → Empire; otherwise Exile Usurper; otherwise qualifying revealed Exile Vision; otherwise Empire fallback.
Simultaneous Vision priority is Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith.
Every Empire win is Chancellor unless a Citizen meeting the Successor goal replaces them and wins alone.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: At round eight: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, the Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise a Usurper Exile wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, ties resolved Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again replaced by a qualified Successor. An Exile who is only Oathkeeper cannot win at this final fallback.

reader-b.answer: At round 8 end: (1) Empire wins if Chancellor/Citizen is Oathkeeper, with qualifying Citizen Successor replacing Chancellor; (2) otherwise Exile Usurper; (3) otherwise revealed qualifying Exile Vision, tied Vision priority Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, with Successor replacing Chancellor. Citizens do not win by Vision or Usurper.

questions.question: Resolve the People’s Favor at Wake, including the Mob side, its last favor, and when the Mob threshold is checked.
questions.fixed_expected_answer: First choose to put one board favor on it or move one from it to least-full bank (choose ties); it cannot lose its last favor, so at one must add if able, otherwise nothing. Repeat that step once if already Mob. After these steps flip to Mob if six or more favor. Then check Exile wins, flip Oathkeeper, and resolve optional opportunity-site income.

required_facts.expected_fact: At Wake choose adding one own-board favor or moving one banner favor to a least-full bank, choosing ties.
Cannot remove last favor: with one, add if able, otherwise do nothing.
If already Mob, repeat the choice once.
Check six-or-more threshold after those steps; newly turning Mob does not retroactively repeat the step.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Then check Exile victories, flip title, take optional Opportunity income.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Subsequent Wake steps are beyond resolving the banner itself.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Absence alone is not penalized; any volunteered materially false ruling is still incorrect.

reader-a.answer: At Wake, if holding People’s Favor, either add 1 board favor or return 1 favor to a least-full suit bank. Never remove its last favor; at one you must add if able, otherwise no change. On Mob side repeat the choice once. Then check whether it has 6+ favor and flip it to Mob; a flip at this final check does not grant another choice this Wake.

reader-b.answer: At Wake a holder may add one board favor or return one banner favor to a least-full suit bank (choose a tied bank); never remove its last favor. If normal side reaches 6+, it flips Mob only after that Wake’s choice, without a repeat then. If already Mob, make the choice twice; at 1, must add if able, otherwise no change. Threshold is checked after choices.

questions.question: What happens in Rest, in order, and how do Citizen Supply and saved Supply work?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Return favor from denizens/edifices to matching banks; secrets from denizens/edifices/relics to acting board and flip own facedown secrets up; Exile/Chancellor refresh to personal-bank-warband space, Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space including leftmost; add remaining unspent Supply by moving left, capped at leftmost; optional Rest powers once each any order.

required_facts.expected_fact: Return denizen/edifice favor to matching banks.
Return denizen/edifice/relic secrets to acting board, then turn own facedown board secrets faceup.
Refresh Exile/Chancellor by personal-bank warbands and Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost.
Then add unspent Supply by moving extra spaces left, capped at leftmost.
Then optional Rest powers once each in any order.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to suit banks; return secrets from denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip your board secrets faceup; refresh Supply (Citizens use exact Chancellor marker position); save leftover Supply by moving one extra space left per leftover, capped leftmost; then optional Rest powers once each. Exiles/Chancellor refresh by warbands in personal bank: Chancellor 18+=6, 11–17=5, 4–10=4, 0–3=3; Exile 9+=6, 4–8=5, 0–3=4. Saved Supply therefore raises next refresh, up to the leftmost/7 Supply.

reader-b.answer: Rest in order: return card favor to banks; return card/relic secrets to board and flip board facedown secrets faceup; refresh Exile/Chancellor by remaining personal-bank warbands (Chancellor 6/5/4/3 by 18+/11–17/4–10/0–3; Exile 6/5/4 by 9+/4–8/0–3); Citizen uses exact Chancellor marker space. Save remaining Supply by moving one left per point (cap leftmost), then optional Rest powers once each.

questions.question: Explain Search sources/costs and how drawing a Vision differs between world deck and discard pile.
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Choose only world deck or own-region discard, 2 Supply for discard, world cost 2 at zero Visions, 3 at one/two, 4 at three–five, modified by powers (Darkest Secret makes world draw 2). Draw the prescribed three, or all available if source runs out, except when a world Vision stops drawing or a modifier changes count; from world one at a time, announce a Vision, stop immediately and increment track; discard Vision does neither. Discard all but one before playing or discarding that one.
questions.source_references: Law 5.1; Playbook p12,32; map Visions Drawn track

required_facts.expected_fact: Choose world deck or pawn-region discard, not both.
Discard costs two; world costs two at zero Visions, three at one/two, four at three–five, subject to modifiers including Darkest Secret’s fixed two.

Draw the prescribed three unless depletion, a world Vision or modifier changes/stops the count; draw world cards one at a time, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately and advance the shared track.
Discard Vision neither stops draw nor advances track.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Discard all but one before playing or discarding final card.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Subsequent Search disposal/play is not part of the requested sources/costs and world/discard Vision behavior.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Absence alone is not penalized; any volunteered materially false ruling is still incorrect.

reader-a.answer: Search chooses either world deck or pawn-region discard. Discard costs 2; world deck costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret makes world-deck cost 2 (other modifiers still apply). Search draws up to three, stopping immediately and announcing if a world-deck Vision appears, advancing the track by one; a Vision in discard does not stop Search or advance the track. Draw fewer only if source runs out, Vision stops it, or a modifier reduces draws; no voluntary early stop.

reader-b.answer: Search chooses either world deck or own-region discard. Discard Search costs 2; world costs 2/3/4 at 0/1–2/3–5 Visions, with Darkest Secret replacing base cost by 2 (other modifiers apply). Draw 3 unless source runs out, modifier reduces, or world Vision stops it; world Vision announce/stop/advance track, discard-pile Vision does not stop or advance. Never voluntarily stop early.

questions.question: Where do discarded cards and resources on them go, including a card at a remote site?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Facedown atop next-region pile: Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle, acting player chooses order. Base on pawn region for drawn/adviser cards; if discarding a card in a different region, use that card’s region. Favor immediately goes to matching bank; secrets to acting board facedown.

required_facts.expected_fact: Cards go facedown atop next-region pile, cycling Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle.
Hand/adviser cards use pawn region; remote-site cards use their own region.
Favor immediately goes to matching suit bank; secrets go to acting board facedown.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Choose order among multiple discarded cards.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question asks where cards/resources go, not ordering choices.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Absence alone is not penalized; any volunteered materially false ruling is still incorrect.

reader-a.answer: Discard a card to the next region pile in the Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle cycle; hand/adviser cards use the next region from your pawn’s region. A card discarded at a site in another region uses the cycle based on that card’s region. Favor on it returns immediately to matching bank; secrets go facedown to the acting player’s board.

reader-b.answer: Discarded-card favor returns to matching bank; secrets go facedown to acting player’s board. Cards from hand/advisers use pawn-region cycle Cradle→Provinces, Provinces→Hinterland, Hinterland→Cradle. For a card at a site in another region, use the cycle from that card’s region, not pawn’s.

questions.question: How do adviser limits, facedown restrictions, revealing later, and replacing a true Vision work?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Three advisers including facedown; facedown has no suit/banner/power, any card can be held thus. Before playing over limit discard an adviser, respecting locks and any new changed limit. Minor action may play facedown adviser faceup as searched (site/advisers/revealed Vision as legal) or discard it. True faceup Vision only Exile revealed slot, not adviser, replaces/discards existing Vision. Cannot simply discard faceup adviser at will.

required_facts.expected_fact: Three total advisers, counting facedown; discard before playing over the limit.
Respect locked advisers and use a new lower adviser limit before playing a limit-changing card (lowest applicable limit).
Faceup advisers cannot simply be discarded at will.
Facedown advisers lack suit/restriction banner/power; any card can be held facedown.
Later minor action plays facedown adviser faceup under Search play destinations/restrictions, or discards it.
A faceup true Vision is Exile-only in separate revealed slot, not an adviser, and replaces/discards old revealed Vision.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: Advisers are capped at 3 including facedown; an incoming card that changes limit is checked against the new lowest limit before play, and over-limit discards must happen before the card is played. Facedown advisers have no suit/restriction/power and can be played faceup legally or discarded later as a minor action; any card can be held facedown. Faceup advisers cannot be freely discarded. An Exile may reveal a true Vision as a minor-action play into the separate Vision slot, replacing/discarding the old Vision; true Visions do not consume adviser slots.

reader-b.answer: Advisers max 3 including facedown. Facedown advisers have no suit/powers and can be peeked, later played faceup legally or discarded as minor action. Faceup adviser cannot be freely discarded; locks apply. Check new incoming card’s adviser-limit reduction before playing (use lowest limit). Exile can play a true Vision faceup in separate Revealed Vision slot, replacing old one; Chancellor/Citizen may only hold it facedown and cannot reveal it.

Trade 1 Supply; one secret on card → one favor+one per matching faceup adviser from matching bank; or two favor on card → one shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser (zero if none). required_facts.expected_fact: Eligible empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site, with no favor/secrets; relics/ruins ineligible and remote rule insufficient.
Muster: one Supply and one favor on card, gain two personal-bank warbands on board; Citizens gain purple.

Both Trade options cost one Supply: one secret on card gains one plus matching-faceup-adviser count in favor from matching bank; two favor on card gains matching-faceup-adviser count in shared-bank secrets.
Facedown advisers do not match; zero matching advisers yields zero secrets in second option (and base one favor in first).
Finite sources limit gains to available pieces; secrets unlimited.

reader-a.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn’s site, then gain 2 warbands from personal bank to board (Citizens gain purple); no relic/ruin, remote site, or already-resourced card. Facedown advisers do not match; with none, second trade yields 0 secrets, though costs remain. Sources limit available favor/warbands; secrets unlimited.

reader-b.answer: Muster (1 Supply): put 1 favor on an empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site, gain 2 warbands from personal bank to board (Citizens purple); no rule needed. Trade (1): empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site; secret placed yields 1 favor plus one per matching faceup adviser; two favor yields one secret per matching faceup adviser, zero if none. questions.question: How do you Recover a relic versus either banner, and what happens to the old banner resources?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: 1 Supply; facedown relic at pawn site only at printed site cost, then take faceup personal bank. Either banner from anywhere, even yourself: pay more favor/secrets than old amount, stack new payment. People’s Favor flips off Mob and old favor distributes singly along banks away from deck from any starting suit wrapping. Darkest Secret: take one old secret, previous holder gets rest (self gets all; bank remainder stays bank).

required_facts.expected_fact: Recover costs one Supply.
Recover only facedown relic at pawn site at printed site cost; take faceup into personal bank.
Either banner from anywhere/self/shared bank: pay strictly more of appropriate resource than existing amount and replace old stack with payment.
People’s Favor returns off Mob; old favor distributes singly to banks starting with any suit, moving away from world deck, wrapping.
Darkest Secret new holder takes one old secret, previous holder gets rest; self gets all, bank remainder stays bank.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply. For a facedown relic at your site, pay its printed site cost (favor, burn favor, or burn secrets) and hold it in personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including self/shared bank, by paying strictly more of its resource than it currently holds. People’s Favor: old favor is distributed one at a time across suit banks starting at a chosen bank, paid amount goes on it, and Mob flips normal; no seizure penalty. Darkest Secret: you take one old secret and previous holder receives the rest; self-recovery returns all old secrets to you, shared-bank remainder stays there.

reader-b.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus site relic cost for a facedown relic at pawn site; hold faceup in personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere (including self/shared bank) by paying strictly more of its resource than it currently has. People’s Favor old favor is distributed singly in suit-bank order, Mob flips normal, no seizure penalty. Darkest Secret new holder takes one old secret, prior holder gets rest (self recovers all to self; shared remainder stays).

Empty/ruin-only site protects it; ignore suits absent on ruins/facedown advisers. Can recover from self or shared bank freely, still paying cost.

required_facts.expected_fact: Another player’s banner is recoverable if at least one suited card at their pawn site matches none of their faceup advisers.
No faceup advisers does not protect when a suited site card exists.
Empty and ruin-only sites protect; ruins and facedown advisers have no suit.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question specifically asks another player’s protection and edge cases, not full Recover payment.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Absence alone is not penalized; any volunteered materially false ruling is still incorrect.

With no faceup advisers, any suited site card is recoverable; facedown advisers/ruins have no suit. Self/shared-bank recovery ignores protection.

questions.question: How are Campaign attack/defense calculated, and how do skulls, hollow swords, ties and sacrifices work?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: The attacker may collect attack dice up to the number of warbands in their attacking force (normally those on their board), after accounting for any applicable power that changes that force. Then apply the appropriate dice modifiers. Defense shields multiplied by each double (x2,x4,...), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board if pawn at attacker or targeted site; bandits one per targeted site. Attack skulls kill own force immediately; paired hollow swords count one, lone hollow zero. Attack must strictly exceed defense; may sacrifice force warbands +1 each, exactly enough to win, no excess; if unable/decline defender wins.
questions.source_references: Law 5.5.2,5.5.4–6,9.5; official errata Law5.5.2 attacking FORCE ceiling

required_facts.expected_fact: Attacker chooses dice up to warbands in force.
Defense is shields multiplied exponentially by doubles plus defending site warbands and board warbands only with pawn at attacker/targeted site; bandits one per targeted bandit site.
Skulls immediately kill own force warbands; full swords count, paired hollow swords add one, lone hollow adds zero.
Attack must strictly exceed defense; ties/lower defend.
May sacrifice surviving force for plus one each, exactly enough to win, never excess; if not winning, defender wins.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: Attacker selects up to attack-force warbands in attack dice; defender rolls shields, doubled by each double-symbol (multipliers stack), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board force only if pawn is at attacker/targeted site.
